would_stop_scrolling: Yes, but only just, and it's the words doing it. 'Did Saudi change its law?' sits right over his face, and I do want to know what a country would change for one man. The picture itself is a guy in a suit at a press table, in a strip across the middle with blur above and below. If that box weren't there I'd keep going.

moments.reaction: Hooked. He says South Africa, he meant Saudi Arabia, and there he is scratching his ear looking caught out. It's funny and he looks like a person. That's the only reason I give it another 30 seconds.
Okay, now I've got reasons to stay. A law rewritten, a whole beach closed for a day. I want to hear both of those. The yellow boxes are easy to read too. This is as interested as I get.

Gone. It started at 30 with 'So who approached first?' Who cares? You just asked me if a country changed its law. Now it's a club president with a name I can't say, a prince, and a tiny timeline card with more names on it. A lot of men in a room and no one to care about. My break is 15 minutes, I'm not spending it on this.

Past where I'd have left. 'His partner Georgina' lands right as she appears, in the white hat with the yellow flowers, and for ten seconds it's about two people and whether they're allowed to live together. This is the video I wanted. It should have been the first minute. Then a FALSE card shows up and it's gone.

Him in the dugout with his hand over his eyes and someone leaning in to comfort him. I've seen a lot of people get bad news, and that looks real to me. I felt it. Four seconds later the voice says 'Forbes' and I'm looking at a bar chart. Let me sit with it for one second, please.

$643,836 a day in the red box. I'll be honest, that got a reaction out of me, because I know what I make for a 12-hour night. But it took 15 seconds of month, week, day, then a four-row table, 'by our arithmetic.' One number would hit harder than the whole spreadsheet.

The 'NO EVIDENCE' card keeps coming back and growing over about 20 seconds until it's a page of small print. The caption reads 'EFE THE BAN.' This is the big answer I waited four minutes for, and it looks like a terms and conditions screen.

The two hands with the rings, filling the whole screen. 'And he did marry her.' That got me, and it's the one shot in the video that's close and quiet. 'Hold on to that one' was three minutes ago, though, and I only remembered it because I went back. Then he's on about goal counts and an investment firm, and the feeling's gone by 284.

felt_cheap_or_ai: Most of the video is a photo in a strip with a blurry copy of itself filling the rest, and after a while it looks like a template. The stand-in pictures are the giveaway: the same tower, skyline and Riyadh-from-space shots keep coming back whenever there's nothing to show, plus what looks like dashcam photos of a Riyadh street, one with the rear-view mirror in it, while they're talking about where a couple lived. Dolphins for the closed beach story was almost funny. A screenshot of a Sports Illustrated web page, twice, feels lazy. The dark cards are the same layout every time with more tiny text than I can read on my phone. Captions chop things where nobody would pause, like 'HOME WAS A FOUR' then 'SEASONS SUITE', or 'ABOUT SIX POINT' then 'THREE FIVE MILLION'. And the voice reads it like a report, with dates all the way down, instead of telling me about anybody.
confusing: The prince, president and minister all blurred together. The 'hugging a painter' and 99 lashes bit comes from nowhere and leaves right away. Who's the painter? Why is that in here? At 203 there's a photo of him with Trump and nobody mentions Trump, and 'its Crown Prince' sounded like the White House had one. Dollars, euros and pounds all get thrown around, and there's an asterisk on the per-game table I never see explained. The most interesting fact about the law, that foreign couples stopped having to prove a relationship to share a hotel room back in 2019, is only in small print on the card. The voice never says it. And 'he made them bend their laws' turned out to be one post someone quoted, which I wouldn't have thought deserved that much of my time.
comment_you_would_post: none, I'd be gone by 40 seconds. If I somehow got to the rings: "4 minutes to find out nobody can prove anything lol. the dugout and the wedding hands were the only parts that felt like real people"
share_or_follow: No share, no save, no follow. I wouldn't send this to my sister. I do trust them, because they keep saying what they couldn't confirm and they refused to label his faith, and that's more careful than most of what's on my feed. But careful isn't the same as caring about someone. By about the fifth 'we found no report' it felt like being walked through their research notes.
one_change: Cut it to about 90 seconds and make it about the couple: she came with him, unmarried, in a country where reports said that was forbidden, people said the law got bent for him, here's what's actually known, the dugout tears, then end on the hands with the rings and don't add anything after them.
